links.comparator_used: Condition 2: LLM reporting based solely on the ultrasound image, with no radiologist report added (Condition 1, radiologist alone, was a further comparator)
links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy, next-step suggestion accuracy and readability of dermatologic ultrasound reports
links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy 83.2% (Condition 3) vs 26.2% (image-only LLM) and 55.4% (radiologist alone), p<0.001; next-step accuracy 77.7% vs 59.9% (image-only LLM) and 38.6% (radiologist alone), p<0.001; readability also highest in Condition 3
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy was highest in Condition 3 (83.2%), compared with Condition 1 (55.4%) and Condition 2 (26.2%) (p<0.001).

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and next-step suggestion accuracy
links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy 83.2% with image plus radiologist report text vs 26.2% with image alone (p<0.001); next-step accuracy 77.7% vs 59.9% (p<0.001)
links.quote: Next-step suggestion accuracy was also highest in Condition 3 (77.7%), followed by Condition 2 (59.9%) and Condition 1 (38.6%) (p<0.001).

design_hint: radiologist-LLM collaboration (LLM combined with radiologist report)
